title: 1 Chronicles 27:16–24
context: The officers over the tribes of Israel, followed by a notice about the census Joab began but did not finish, which looks back to 1 Chronicles 21 and 2 Samuel 24. Questions about God’s role in that census are treated at the Judges 9:23 key contrast.

verses.text: Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri was the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.arminianNotes: Over the tribes: Eliezer son of Zichri for Reuben, Shephatiah son of Maacah for Simeon. Arminian readers see tribal leadership maintained alongside the army divisions.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see David’s administration respecting tribal structure. The list of tribal officers complements the military roster and shows a well-ordered kingdom.

verses.text: of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok;
verses.arminianNotes: For Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok. Arminian readers see the priestly line given its own representative among the tribal leaders.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Levi and Aaron listed separately, reflecting their distinct roles. Zadok’s mention connects this list with his prominent priestly role elsewhere in the narrative.

verses.text: of Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
verses.arminianNotes: For Judah, Elihu, “one of the brothers of David”; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael. Arminian readers see David’s family included in tribal leadership.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note Elihu’s relation to David. Some interpreters connect him with Eliab, David’s eldest brother, though readers in this tradition hold the identification tentatively.

verses.text: of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel;
verses.arminianNotes: For Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jeremoth son of Azriel. Arminian readers see northern tribes represented in David’s administration.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the inclusion of all Israel. The list continues to record each tribe’s leader, showing the comprehensive scope of David’s rule.

verses.text: of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
verses.arminianNotes: For Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for half of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah. Arminian readers see the Joseph tribes given leaders within the kingdom’s structure.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the careful division of Manasseh into its two parts. The record reflects the tribal arrangements established in the land.

verses.text: of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
verses.arminianNotes: For half of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner. Arminian readers see even Saul’s tribe led by the son of Saul’s former commander.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise note Jaasiel’s possible connection to Abner, Saul’s general, though the identification is not certain. The list suggests reconciliation within David’s kingdom.

verses.text: of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the captains of the tribes of Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: For Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham; “These were the captains of the tribes of Israel.” Arminian readers see the tribal list completed and summarized.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the closing summary of tribal leaders. Readers in this tradition note that Gad and Asher are not named in this list, an omission the text does not explain.

verses.text: But David didn’t take the number of them from twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.
verses.arminianNotes: David did not count those twenty and under, “because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.” Arminian readers see a reminder of the promise in Genesis 15:5.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s promise shaping the record. The verse looks back to the census of chapter 21 and 2 Samuel 24, whose motive Scripture does not state and which is not explained further here.

verses.text: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and wrath came on Israel for this. The number wasn’t put into the account in the chronicles of King David.
verses.arminianNotes: “Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and wrath came on Israel for this.” Arminian readers see the census remembered as bringing judgment, consistent with 2 Samuel 24.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the notice pointing back to the judgment in 1 Chronicles 21 and 2 Samuel 24. Questions of God’s role and evil agents there are treated at the Judges 9:23 box, not repeated here.
